root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Anti-Tartakower Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 d5 4. Nc3 Be7 5. Bg5 O-O 6. e3 h6 7. Bxf6

overview: White trades the g5 bishop for the f6 knight (7.Bxf6) and keeps the c4/d4 pressure; after ...Bxf6 Black plays ...c6 and ...Nd7 or ...dxc4 and White uses Rc1 or Qb3 for a small space edge. Black has the bishop pair-like activity of the f6 bishop and solid defences, and the game is slow and manoeuvring.

white_ideas.idea: Rc1 and Qb3 pressure against c6/d5
Bd3 and castling, then cxd5 or Bxc4 after ...dxc4
Hold a small space advantage with the c4/d4 centre

black_ideas.idea: Free the position with ...dxc4 and ...e5 or ...c5
Keep the pawn chain compact and avoid weaknesses

typical_structures.structure: QGD d5/e6 chain with White c4/d4 and e3
After ...dxc4 Bxc4 a symmetrical-looking centre with ...e5 or ...c5 breaks

character.notes: Known as a safe QGD set-up with an early piece trade; few ways for either side to go wrong quickly.

gambit.notes: No material is given on purpose in the main line.

soundness.notes: A main-line QGD set-up, fully sound.

structure.notes: Centre in tension; Black ...dxc4 or ...c6 and e-pawn breaks decide it. Standard QGD flexibility.

approach.notes: Mainstream QGD branch, not a system.

level.notes: Slow manoeuvring play where plans matter more than theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Gligoric Variation
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 h6 7. Bxf6 Bxf6 8. Rc1
sublines_that_differ.how: Rc1 pressure on c6 and a quicker c-file build-up.

character.reason: Orthodox QGD set-up with early trades and no forcing play.

structure.reason: QGD centre in tension, as in the anchors.

approach.reason: A normal QGD move order, not a system.

level.reason: Plans matter more than lines to memorise.

plans.reason: No single plan stands out from memory.
